reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: All 3 gates passed. An attacker can trigger this via the public `liquidate` entry point by calling `refresh_usd_price` during a genuine spot-price spike (e.g., debt token spot 10% above EMA), then immediately calling `liquidate`: the health check in `ensure_liquidate_borrow_allowed` uses EMA prices (`get_price`, L998/L1115/L1155) so the position qualifies, but `liquidate_calculate_seize_ctokens` uses `get_spot_price` (L1045-1046) — inflating seized collateral by ~21% excess per step relative to EMA-based intent; after the first step the close-factor bypass threshold (collateral ≤ 1.01 × debt, L988) can be crossed, allowing subsequent liquidation steps to fully drain remaining collateral. The inconsistency is confirmed in code: non-liquidation borrow/withdraw paths enforce EMA/spot tolerance via `get_price_with_check` (L1198, L1284), but the seizure path has no such guard.
